title: Zero locus of a section over a valuation base is relative Cartier
statement: Let A be a valuation ring, let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be proper, flat, and of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let x_0 be a closed point of \operatorname{Spec}(A), and let X_0 be the fibre over x_0, assumed integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let L be an invertible module on X [def-sc-invertible-module], and let s be a global section of L whose restriction to X_0 is nonzero. Then the zero scheme Z(s) [def-pc-zero-scheme] is a relative effective Cartier divisor on X over \operatorname{Spec}(A) [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], hence Z(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) is flat.

proof.text: Let phi be homOfGlobalSection M s. Use the local-principality, pullback and zero-iff facts of lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties directly in their upstream morphism formulations Hom.isLocallyPrincipal_zeroLocus, Hom.comap_zeroLocus and Hom.zeroLocus_eq_bot_iff. The ideal J = phi.zeroLocus is locally principal. If its comap to the closed fibre were bottom, the ordinary pulled-back morphism would be zero. Naturality of the ordinary pullback adjunction unit, evaluated on 1, would then make the ordinary restriction of s zero. Compare the tensorPullback adjunction of lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction with the ordinary adjunction using leftAdjointUniq and unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. Its component is an isomorphism, hence injective on sections, contradicting hs0. Thus the closed-fibre ideal is nonzero and locally principal. Apply lem-pc-nonzero-locally-principal-ideal-invertible on the integral fibre to get its invertibility.

The specified closed point is the unique closed point of the valuation ring. For each x in the support of J, properness gives a closed map (lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image); its specializingMap lifts specialization of f(x) to the closed point to x specializing to y over that point. Closedness of support puts y in J.support. Apply fibre_cartier_local using local principality and the invertible closed-fibre ideal. Its open neighbourhood of y also contains x. Outside J.support, restrict to its open complement; the ideal there is top, locally generated by the regular element 1, and its subscheme is empty, hence flat.

Choose the resulting open neighbourhood for every point; they cover X. Glue invertibility by IsInvertible.of_iSup_opensRange_eq_top. The inverse images of these opens cover J.subscheme. Identify each restricted subscheme with the subscheme of the comapped ideal using comapIso, pullbackSymmetry and pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict; transport local flatness across this isomorphism. Glue flatness by IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_iSup_eq_top. These two conclusions are exactly IsRelativeEffectiveCartier, including flatness of J.subscheme to Spec A.

lean.statement: theorem valuation_zero_section_relative_cartier (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x₀ : Spec (.of A)) (hx₀ : IsClosed ({x₀} : Set (Spec (.of A)))) [IsIntegral (f.fiber x₀)] (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (s : Γ(M, ⊤)) (hs₀ : ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (f.fiberι x₀))).unit.app M).val.app (op ⊤) s ≠ 0) : Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsRelativeEffectiveCartier (Scheme.Modules.Hom.zeroLocus (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection M s)) f
